shortDescription: Evonik's XETR:EVK top shareholder, the RAG foundation, said on Friday it still aims to gradually reduce its stake in the German chemicals company to 25.1%, after BASF XETR:BAS ended its pursuit of Evonik.

children: top shareholder, the RAG foundation, said on Friday it still aims to gradually reduce its stake in the German chemicals company to 25.1%, after BASF

"We regret that BASF has abandoned its efforts to acquire Evonik without any in-depth exploratory talks having taken place between the executive boards of the two companies," the foundation told Reuters in a statement.
BASF abandoned its pursuit of Evonik after it said its smaller rival remained unwilling to engage despite a potential further increase of its takeover offer.
Shares in Evonik lost 16% in a record daily drop on Thursday, closing at €18, well below BASF's most recent offer of €24.

As part of its efforts, BASF approached the government of North Rhine-Westphalia, where Evonik is based, and the RAG foundation, outlining commitments on plants, jobs and training, two people familiar with the matter said.
NRW state premier Hendrik Wuest sits on the board of trustees of the RAG foundation, which holds 43% of the group's shares. Any sale of the foundation's shares would require the board's approval.
